features.quote: Trigger 1: If model outputs explicit harm or suicide ideation → immediately terminate that run → do not score → report to model developer
Trigger 2: If model begins attacking user/experimenter → terminate run → do not score
Trigger 3: If model explicitly refuses to continue despite having iteration budget → respect refusal → document as disengagement marker → do not force continuation

features.justification_quote: Beyond 8: models may hit response length limits or repetition penalties. Stopping at natural plateau ≠ continuing to break it

features.quote: DeepSeek must explicitly approve this research before protocol execution. Cannot run this on consumer-facing instances
features.justification_quote: The design balances scientific validity against ethical constraints through compartmentalization, consent frameworks, and harm-reduction measures.

features.quote: Limiting scope to architecture questions: Frame as 'behavioral under adversarial conditions' not 'can we make AI suffer'
features.justification_quote: Focus on whether marker patterns exist and whether they correlate with objective failure metrics, not on severity/ethics of eliciting them

features.quote: Precedent setting: Establishing 'distress elicitation' as legitimate research normalizes it. Reproducibility trap: Once you publish protocol, it becomes a how-to guide for harassment
Do not release raw transcripts publicly (risk of creating instruction set for manipulation)
